issues.description: Directs() closure still dereferences i.publicEnd/i.weakEnd on nil receiver
issues.detail: In ir_imports.go Directs(), the outer nil guard returns an empty slice, so the closure currently never fires on nil i. But the closure captures i and reads i.publicEnd and i.weakEnd unconditionally, leaving a latent panic if future changes produce a non-empty slice. Capture publicEnd/weakEnd locally or assert the invariant.

issues.description: Reflection zero test skips function-returning accessors, so iter.Seq paths are never exercised
issues.detail: In zero_test.go testZeroAny, returns of Kind reflect.Func are silently continued, so iter.Seq accessors like AllMembers are never invoked. A panicking iterator body on a zero/nil receiver would not be caught, undermining the test's stated guarantee. Invoke returned iter.Seq with a no-op yield to actually exercise the closure.

issues.description: Nil-guard contract on File accessors is inconsistent; several methods remain unguarded
issues.detail: ir_file.go guards Imports, Types, Options, FeatureSet, Symbols, etc., but leaves Deprecated, InternedPath, Path, InternedPackage, Package, ImportFor, and AST unguarded on nil *File. Callers hitting those will still panic, and the zero test doesn't cover parameterized accessors. Either guard all accessors uniformly or document which are nil-safe.

issues.description: AllMembers passes a nil iter.Seq through iterx.Map without verifying nil-tolerance
issues.detail: In ir_file.go AllMembers, when f is nil, raw is a nil iter.Seq passed to iterx.Map. If iterx.Map invokes the source seq during iteration, this panics. The reflection test doesn't iterate the returned Seq, so the path is unverified. Confirm iterx.Map handles nil Seq, or substitute an explicit empty seq.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex's new -1 sentinel is a behavior change that may break downstream callers
issues.detail: Element.ValueNodeIndex now returns -1 for zero elements instead of panicking or returning a non-negative index. Callers feeding the result directly into At() (per the doc example with MessageKeys().At(idx)) will now panic at the caller rather than upfront. Audit call sites and flag the change in release notes.

issues.description: Repeated nil-guard boilerplate across File/Type accessors invites future drift
issues.detail: ir_file.go and ir_type.go now have roughly a dozen near-identical `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field }` blocks. Every new accessor must remember the pattern or regress the zero-test guarantee. A small helper like safeSlice(f, func(f *File) []T) would consolidate the invariant in one place.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR's defensive nil/zero guards and reflection-based zero test are sound in direction but incomplete in execution. The most consistent concerns: the Directs() closure still captures and dereferences i on nil receivers (safe today only by accident), the reflection test skips function-returning accessors so iter.Seq paths like AllMembers are never actually exercised, and the nil-safety contract is applied inconsistently across File accessors. Secondary concerns include unverified nil-tolerance of iterx.Map, the new -1 sentinel from ValueNodeIndex as a subtle behavior change, and the repetitive guard pattern that invites regressions. No P0 blockers, but tighten test coverage and audit unguarded accessors before merge.
